name: biogears_resuscitation
description: Hemorrhage in the real BioGears engine with a closed-loop MAP-targeted IV fluid controller.

state_file.description: BioGears state in <runtime>/states (or an absolute path)

conditions.description: Chronic conditions applied while the patient stabilizes, e.g. {ChronicAnemia: {ReductionFactor: 0.3}}

circuit_additions.description: New path name -> {source, target, resistance_mmHg_s_per_mL} added to the cardiovascular circuit with its compartment link (a perturbation)

rate_mL_per_min.description: Initial bleeding rate; BioGears' rate then falls with local pressure

time_step_s.description: BioGears' solver step (validated at 0.02 s; must be < 0.1 s)

compound.description: Infused compound (a BioGears compound, e.g. Saline, Blood_ONegative)

biogears.doc:
Time-stepped bridge to the real BioGears 8.2.0 engine.

The engine is loaded from a BioGears state file (``state_file``, a name in
``<runtime>/states`` or an absolute path) on first use and advanced by
``interval`` seconds on every update. Interventions arrive as setpoints on the
input ports and are forwarded to BioGears as actions only when they change.

Inputs
------
hemorrhage_rate_mL_per_min : overwrite[float]
    Initial bleeding rate at ``config.hemorrhage_compartment``; 0 stops the
    bleed. BioGears' bleed rate falls with the local pressure from this initial
    value. It must stay below cardiac output: BioGears refuses a larger rate on
    every step without stopping, which this process raises as an error.
iv_rate_mL_per_min : overwrite[float]
    Infusion rate of ``config.iv_compound`` (e.g. Saline, Blood_ONegative); 0 stops it.

Outputs
-------
Vital signs (see ``VITALS``) as ``overwrite[float]``: ``initial_state()``
seeds each store with the loaded state's reading and every update emits
BioGears' current reading, so the store always equals BioGears' own value.
The engine starts from ``state_file`` or a ``patient_file`` (``viva_biogears.patients``).
A state saved mid-run (``save_state_times_s``, ``viva_biogears.states``) carries its
bleed and infusion; the setpoints start at their values, so the same setpoints
continue the run and different ones send the change.

``irreversible_state`` turns True once BioGears reports its irreversible state
(it does at 50 % blood loss); the engine is not advanced after that, so the
vitals stores keep the last reading BioGears produced.

emitter.doc:
Store historical states in memory.

``subsample`` records only every Nth composite tick (default 1 =
every tick). Use this for long runs or composites with heavy
state (large fields, many agents) to keep RAM bounded — the
saved time-series still reflects the simulation's true cadence
via each row's ``global_time`` field.

``max_len`` optionally bounds ``history`` to the most recent N
recorded rows (a ring buffer): once the cap is reached each new
record drops the oldest. Default ``None`` = unbounded (the
historical behaviour — consumers such as v2ecoli that read the
full ``history`` are unaffected unless they opt in). ``max_len``
counts *recorded* rows (i.e. post-``subsample``).

_contract.description: type(name, bases, dict, **kwds) -> a new type

controller.doc:
Proportional fluid-resuscitation controller on mean arterial pressure.

Sets the IV infusion rate in proportion to how far MAP is below
``target_map_mmHg``, clipped to ``[0, max_rate_mL_per_min]``. It writes a
setpoint, so its output port is ``overwrite[float]``.
